description: What the Celestia nodes that Unity Nodes runs actually use, measured on its own servers and shown beside Celestia's recommended hardware, from Unity Nodes Pulse: CPU cores (median, 95th percentile and maximum), RAM of the processes, network and disk I/O (median and 95th percentile) the data size with its change per day, an estimate of the network traffic per month, and for the Fibre service how full its shard store is against its budget and how many shards it uploaded and served in the window (successful and failed apart), for each node role that has a node (validator, consensus node, bridge, Fibre, light node, Fibre included on mainnet and on Mocha), each node named by its role and CPU, over 1, 7 or 30 days. Measured values, with clearly labelled estimates kept apart from them (a straight-line projection of each node's data size, the Celestia Foundation's Fibre calculator for Unity Nodes' voting power and, on mainnet, Celestia's own planning scenario for bridge data): the chain's own load in the same window (block data per second at the median, 95th percentile and maximum) beside the block limit read from the chain, the average block time and how much of that capacity the load fills, with a correlation r of each node's CPU, network and disk load with it (a link in how they moved, not a cause; shown once four hours overlap), and the answer says how much of the window the samples fill (the fewest samples of any node times the step, with a gap or a late start in the data named), so early figures are provisional. For what Celestia's documentation requires, use search or get_doc ("Hardware requirements"); for servers that meet it, list_datacenter_offers; for an estimate of Fibre load, size_fibre_node. Celestia only.

role.description: Only this node role; all roles when left out

window.description: 1d, 7d or 30d: the span the median, 95th percentile and maximum cover

name: get_celestia_hardware_usage
